description: Ur featured a massive ziggurat complex at its center, with dense residential neighborhoods connected by narrow winding streets. The harbor district provided access to trade via the Euphrates.
reconstruction_notes: Extensively excavated by Woolley in the 1920s-30s. Ziggurat partially reconstructed.

street_pattern: orthogonal grid with main east-west and north-south avenues
description: Mohenjo-daro exemplifies Indus Valley urban planning with its strict grid layout, advanced drainage system, and the Great Bath. The citadel mound and lower city show clear functional zoning.
reconstruction_notes: UNESCO World Heritage site. Great Bath and granary well-preserved.

street_pattern: strict grid aligned 15.5 degrees east of north
description: Teotihuacan's Avenue of the Dead served as the central axis, flanked by the Pyramids of the Sun and Moon. Apartment compounds housed multi-family units in a planned residential system.
reconstruction_notes: Avenue of the Dead and major pyramids excavated. Many apartment compounds mapped.

street_pattern: organic with agora as focal point
description: Classical Athens grew organically around the Acropolis and Agora. The Long Walls to Piraeus ensured maritime access. Residential areas featured courtyard houses along narrow streets.
reconstruction_notes: Extensive archaeological record. Agora excavated by American School.

street_pattern: radiating from Forum with grid in newer districts
description: Rome evolved from a hilltop settlement to a vast metropolis. The Forum served as political and commercial center. Elaborate infrastructure included 11 aqueducts, the Cloaca Maxima sewer, and extensive road network.
reconstruction_notes: Continuous habitation complicates archaeology. Forum and Colosseum extensively studied.

description: Chang'an under the Tang dynasty was the world's largest city, with a strict grid of walled wards, two major markets, and the imperial palace complex at the north. The city plan reflected cosmological principles.
reconstruction_notes: Modern Xi'an overlies most of the Tang city. Some walls and gates excavated.

street_pattern: grid-like with canals as organizing axes
fortification_type: moat and laterite walls around Angkor Thom
description: Angkor's urban landscape centered on temple-mountains like Angkor Wat and the Bayon. An elaborate hydraulic system of barays (reservoirs) and canals supported rice agriculture and urban life.
reconstruction_notes: LIDAR surveys revealed vast low-density urban sprawl. Temple restorations ongoing.

street_pattern: grid with canals as streets and causeways
fortification_type: lake location served as natural defense
description: Tenochtitlan was built on an island in Lake Texcoco, connected by causeways. Chinampas (floating gardens) extended the city. The Templo Mayor dominated the sacred precinct at the center.
reconstruction_notes: Templo Mayor excavated in 1978. Colonial accounts by Cortes and Diaz provide details.

fortification_type: massive dry-stone walls up to 11m high
description: Great Zimbabwe featured the Great Enclosure with its iconic conical tower, the Hill Complex (royal residence), and the Valley Ruins. Dry-stone construction without mortar demonstrates sophisticated masonry.
reconstruction_notes: Extensively studied since 1890s. Great Enclosure and Hill Complex well-documented.

street_pattern: organic with mosque and market as anchors
description: Timbuktu served as a major center of Islamic scholarship and trans-Saharan trade. The Djinguereber, Sankore, and Sidi Yahia mosques anchored distinct quarters. The city's wealth derived from gold and salt trade.
reconstruction_notes: Three great mosques still standing. Many manuscripts preserved in private libraries.

street_pattern: radial from central plaza with roads to four suyus
description: Cusco was planned in the shape of a puma, with Sacsayhuaman as the head. The Coricancha (Temple of the Sun) was the religious center. Four main roads led to the four quarters of Tawantinsuyu.
reconstruction_notes: Spanish colonial city built over Inca foundations. Coricancha partially preserved beneath Santo Domingo.

description: Tell es-Sultan (ancient Jericho) represents one of the earliest permanent settlements. The pre-pottery Neolithic town featured a massive stone wall and tower, suggesting organized defense and labor coordination.
reconstruction_notes: Kenyon's excavations revealed PPNA levels. Tower and wall well-documented.

fortification_type: no walls - continuous house exterior served as perimeter
description: Catalhoyuk featured densely packed mudbrick houses entered from the roof. Interior walls were decorated with murals and bull skulls. No formal streets existed; movement was across rooftops.
reconstruction_notes: UNESCO World Heritage site. Excavations by Mellaart and later Hodder.

description: Persepolis was built on a massive stone terrace, featuring the Apadana (audience hall), the Gate of All Nations, and elaborate relief carvings. It served as ceremonial capital of the Achaemenid Empire.
reconstruction_notes: Excavated by Herzfeld and Schmidt. Relief carvings well-preserved.

street_pattern: organic with cothon (circular military harbor) as focal feature
fortification_type: triple wall system on landward side
description: Carthage featured a unique circular military harbor (cothon) and rectangular commercial harbor. The Byrsa hill held the citadel. Multi-story residential buildings and elaborate cistern systems characterized the city.
reconstruction_notes: Largely destroyed by Rome in 146 BCE. UNESCO excavations revealed Punic levels.
